result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks, traffic signals, and continuous sidewalks on both sides. However, the presence of streetcar tracks in the roadway and wide crossing distances without refuge islands or curb extensions increases risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Streetcar tracks
hazards.description: Metal tracks embedded in the roadway can be slippery when wet and present a tripping hazard for pedestrians crossing the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Running through the center and right side of the intersection roadway

hazards.name: Visibility obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk can obscure the view between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb on the left side of the image

hazards.name: Degraded pavement
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven pavement near the tracks and crosswalk area increases the risk of trips.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The street environment includes continuous sidewalks and signalized intersections in a mixed-use urban area. Pedestrian safety is hindered by faded pavement markings, poor road surface conditions including embedded rail tracks, and a lack of physical separation from traffic.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk at the intersection is significantly worn, reducing its visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Poor pavement condition
hazards.description: The roadway surface shows significant cracking and wear, which can create tripping hazards or affect vehicle braking.

hazards.name: Embedded rail tracks
hazards.description: Trolley tracks in the roadway can be slippery when wet and pose a tripping hazard for pedestrians or a crash risk for cyclists.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace faded transverse markings with continental or ladder-style high-visibility markings.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Street trees
interventions.description: Install street trees or planters between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

result.summary: The street features a wide roadway with embedded tram tracks and parallel parking on both sides, which likely encourages higher vehicle speeds. While sidewalks are present, the environment lacks marked crossings, pedestrian safety infrastructure, and buffers between the walkway and moving traffic.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The excessive width of the asphalt roadway, including the tram track area, encourages higher vehicle speeds and increases pedestrian crossing distance.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street creates sightline barriers between pedestrians and approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Embedded Tram Tracks
hazards.description: The metal tracks embedded in the pavement can be a tripping hazard for pedestrians and a slip/fall hazard for cyclists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at intersections to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked, high-visibility crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed cushions or other vertical deflection measures to slow vehicle speeds on this wide residential street.

result.summary: The image shows a typical residential street with row houses and continuous sidewalks on both sides. While sidewalks are present, they are relatively narrow and partially obstructed by utility poles, and the presence of parked cars on both sides creates significant visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked vehicles on both sides of the street obscures the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians, particularly children, who might step into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbsides throughout the foreground and midground.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly within the narrow sidewalk path, reducing the effective clear width for pedestrians and those using mobility devices.
hazards.location_in_image: Large wooden utility pole on the left side of the sidewalk in the center foreground.
